title: Capacity projection matrix by region & GPU mix — Q3 2026
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures the capacity projection matrix for Q3 2026 across NA / EU / APAC, showing recommended GPU mixes, utilization targets (P50/P90), buffers, and a phased rollout timeline for new regions and burst pools. The goal is to produce a single actionable plan for procurement, region enablement, and autoscaling policies that SRE, Serving Runtime, and Capacity Planning can execute on for the next quarter.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
We anticipate a +28–40% increase in peak inference throughput demand from mid-March to end of September driven by increased hosted-api customers and two enterprise Dedicated contracts coming online. To meet latency SLAs while controlling cost, we recommend a mixed GPU procurement that prioritizes H100 for EU/NA baseline capacity, L4 for low-latency embedding routes in NA and APAC, and a small A100 spot pool for burst capacity in EU. Reserve lead-time purchases in Q2 with staged region enablement: NA baseline -> EU baseline -> APAC ramp. Target fleet utilization: P50 68% (steady-state), P90 84% (peak), maintain 12–18% hot spare buffer per region.

Key assumptions:
- Demand growth: conservative +28% (P50) to aggressive +40% (P90) for token throughput Sept vs Mar.
- Average session length and token generation distribution based on March evals (median 65 tokens; 95th pct 420 tokens).
- Autoscaler achieves 6x vertical burst but requires baseline capacity for <150ms cold-start SLOs.
- Procurement lead times: 8–12 weeks for reserved H100 nodes; 4–6 weeks for L4/T4.
- Cross-region fallback allowed for non-latency-sensitive workloads up to 200ms extra RTT.

Projection matrix (by region, Q3 2026 target fleet):
Columns: Region | Baseline GPUs (Q3 target) | GPU Mix | P50 util | P90 util | Hot-spare buffer | Notes
- NA | 1,200 GPUs | 48% H100 / 32% L4 / 20% A100-burst | 65% | 82% | 15% | Priority baseline; host new Dedicated block for fintech customer (ENG-1423).
- EU | 900 GPUs | 60% H100 / 10% L4 / 30% A100-spot | 70% | 86% | 18% | Sensitive to procurement lead time; plan A100 spot for quick capacity.
- APAC | 420 GPUs | 20% H100 / 60% L4 / 20% L4-large | 62% | 80% | 12% | Start with L4-heavy fleet for cost and region latency; H100 baseline as demand solidifies.

GPU-type rationale and role:
- H100: Primary for long-context chat and high-QPS customer routes requiring best throughput. Use as baseline in NA/EU where large enterprise SLAs exist.
- A100 (reserved/spot): Use as burst pool for unpredictable traffic spikes and regression windows; cheaper in some clouds and compatible with runtime fallback.
- L4/T4: Cost-efficient for embeddings, short generations, and APAC latency-sensitive traffic; enables lower unit cost on high-volume embedding workloads.

Scenario planning (three scenarios):
- Base (P50 growth +28%): Current procurement plan (orders placed) sufficient; minor rebalancing between NA/EU.
- Upside (P75 ~34%): Activate A100-spot pools and increase autoscaler headroom; delay low-priority batch jobs to off-peak windows.
- Stress (P90 ~40%): Temporarily route non-latency-critical hosted customers to cross-region fallback; activate emergency spot purchases and short-term cloud credits.

Rollout & procurement timeline (quarter view — July to September 2026):
- Week 1–4 (Jul): Confirm reserved H100 order quantities for NA & EU (PO sent by Procurement). Finalize rack/software configs. Jira: ENG-1558.
- Week 5–8 (Aug): L4 fleet deploys in APAC (initial 200 GPUs). Autoscaler tuning and KV-cache warmup testing.
- Week 9–12 (Sep): A100 burst pool activation in EU and NA; smoke test canary traffic and measure tail latencies.
- Contingency (rolling): If any procurement slip >2 weeks, shift 10–20% non-critical capacity to cross-region routing and increase burst spot budget by up to 30%.

Operational playbook snippets:
- Region admission gating: Only enable a model variant in a region after 48h of synthetic traffic showing P99 latency <1.5x baseline.
- Autoscaler knobs: target_token_rate_per_gpu=95% of bench rate; max_concurrent_shards per node reduced by 10% during first 72h after new pool attach.
- Cache warmup: schedule prefix-cache seeding for top 100 routes 24h before customer cutover.

Risks and mitigations:
- Procurement delays: pre-authorize a spot-pool budget for month-to-month cloud spikes; maintain list of 3 alternate instance shapes.
- Unexpected traffic patterns: keep a 10% emergency reserved capacity that is not scheduled for Dedicated customers.
- Inter-region network incidents: define a static fallback mapping for non-sensitive endpoints to route to nearest alternative region; update DNS TTL to 60s for fast failover.

Open decisions (ask list):
- Approve increased spot budget from $120k/month to $160k/month during Q3 ramp? (Finance approval needed).
- Final H100/ L4 ratio for NA after Dedicated contract onboarding (decision deadline: 2026-03-20).

Action items (short):
- Asha: finalize procurement POs for H100 NA/EU (due 2026-03-16).
- Daniel: run autoscaler soak test with 30% synthetic peak traffic and report latency histograms (ENG-1569).
- Marta: prepare runbook for APAC L4 rollout and identify rack space constraints (OPS-89).

Appendix — quick capacity table (numbers are targets, rounded):
- NA: H100 576 | L4 384 | A100-burst 240 | Total 1,200
- EU: H100 540 | L4 90 | A100-spot 270 | Total 900
- APAC: H100 84 | L4 252 | L4-large 84 | Total 420

Notes & references:
- This is a working sheet; numbers will be refined once we receive final telemetry for March–May and Procurement confirms lead times.
- Related: ENG-1423 (fintech Dedicated on-boarding), PR infra-config/217 (region templates).

Document history: created 2026-03-10 by Asha Kapoor, collaborators Daniel Park and Marta Ruiz. Last modified 2026-03-12 after autoscaler test preliminary results.
